nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec policy and regulatory considerations_qna_000
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What socio-economic aspects of nuclear energy are discussed in the collection?
nodes.answer: Perspectives on market readiness, legal frameworks, and international cooperation in nuclear energy are discussed.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec policy and regulatory considerations_qna_001
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: What must happen before new nuclear reactor concepts can be commercially implemented in the U.S.?
nodes.answer: New nuclear reactor concepts must be approved for licensing by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec policy and regulatory considerations_qna_002
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What action did OECD countries take regarding export finance for coal-fired power projects in 2015?
nodes.answer: OECD countries agreed to restrict export finance for coal-fired power projects in 2015.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec policy and regulatory considerations_qna_003
nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: What factors affect the capacity of Export Credit Agencies (ECAs) to support renewable energy industries?
nodes.answer: The capacity of ECAs to respond to demand for export credit from renewable energy industries is contingent on having policy tools that support renewables firms, which may have different needs than firms in oil, gas, and coal industries.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec policy and regulatory considerations_qna_004
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: How have domestic content requirements, investment support, and risk aversion affected ECAs in the US and UK?
nodes.answer: In the US and UK, domestic content requirements, investment support, and risk aversion have all affected the extent to which Exlm and UKEF have supported renewable industries.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec policy and regulatory considerations_qna_005
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What action did OECD countries take in 2015 regarding export finance for coal-fired power projects?
nodes.answer: OECD countries agreed to restrict export finance for coal-fired power projects in 2015.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec policy and regulatory considerations_qna_006
nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How have domestic policies in the US and UK impacted ECAs' support for renewable industries?
nodes.answer: Domestic content requirements, investment support, and risk aversion have all influenced the extent to which ECAs like Exlm (Export-Import Bank of the United States) and UKEF (UK Export Finance) have supported renewable industries.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec policy and regulatory considerations_qna_007
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What factors shape the capacity of Exlm and UKEF to promote renewable energy exports?
nodes.answer: The extent of political control over the bureaucracy, the size and composition of green industrial bases, and the policy tools available to both ECAs.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Clean energy|Ocean thermal energy|Otec policy and regulatory considerations_qna_008
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What agreement did OECD countries reach in 2015 regarding export finance?
nodes.answer: OECD countries agreed to restrict export finance for coal-fired power projects in 2015.
